title: Schema Design Patterns
subtitle: Designing flexible yet efficient MongoDB schemas

content.text: Even though MongoDB is schema-free, good schema design is critical for performance. The key question: embed or reference?

content.definition: Storing related data inside the same document. Reduces joins but can bloat documents.
Storing the _id of related documents and looking them up separately. Equivalent to SQL foreign keys.

content.text: Embed when data is queried together. Reference when data is updated independently or is very large.

questions.question: When should you embed a document instead of referencing?
options: When the sub-document is shared across many documents
When data is always queried together and rarely changes independently
When the array can grow unboundedly
questions.explanation: Embedding is best when the related data is always read together and belongs to one parent.

faq.q: Can a MongoDB document have size limits?
faq.a: Yes. A single document cannot exceed 16 MB. For large arrays that grow over time, referencing is safer.
